name: Spiced apple and granola cake with salted honey buttercream
ingredients: 100 millilitre Scottish honey from highland heather
3 tablespoon Scottish honey from highland heather
method: To make the apple puree for the cake, place the frozen Bramley apple slices (250 g) into a medium pan with a tablespoon of water. Cook over a medium heat for 15–20 minutes, until soft enough to purée, stirring occasionally to prevent it sticking and burning. Purée with a stick blender or in the small bowl of a food processor. Set aside.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas mark 4. Line a loaf tin with greaseproof paper.

Beat the unsalted butter (115 g) and soft light brown sugar (100 g) until light and fluffy. Beat in the Scottish honey from highland heather (100 millilitre) and the large egg (1) and stir in the cooked apples.

In a separate bowl, sift the  plain flour (225 g), bicarbonate of soda (1 1/2 tsp), baking powder (1 tsp), ground cinnamon (1 tsp), ground ginger (1 tsp) and a generous pinch of salt. Fold the flour into the wet mixture. Stop mixing as soon as they are combined (it will be thick), then stir in the nut and raisin granola (100 g).
Scrape the batter into the lined tin. Bake for 40–50 minutes, or until an inserted skewer comes out clean and the surface of the cake feels springy when pressed. Cool in the tin.

Meanwhile, make the buttercream. Beat the salted butter (125 g) until light and fluffy, add the Scottish honey from highland heather (3 tbsp) and gradually beat in the icing sugar (200 g) until light and fluffy. Spread over the cake and scatter with nut and raisin granola (1 handful).
